# dify Provider

The Dify provider manages Dify applications, model and tool provider credentials, plugin installs, and app API keys as infrastructure-as-code via Terraform. It authenticates with a Personal Access Token against the workspace-scoped OpenAPI.

## Authentication

Create a Personal Access Token in the Dify console: **account settings → Personal Access Tokens**. The token acts as your user account, so it must have access to the workspace you manage — including workspace-scoped permissions for the operations you run (app import/export, credential management, plugin install, and so on). Treat it like a password: it is stored in Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    dify = {
      source = "registry.terraform.io/dify/dify"
    }
  }
}

# All attributes can also be set via environment variables:
#   DIFY_HOST, DIFY_TOKEN, DIFY_WORKSPACE_ID
provider "dify" {
  host         = "https://dify.example.com"
  token        = var.dify_token
  workspace_id = var.dify_workspace_id
}

variable "dify_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "dify_workspace_id" {
  type    = string
  default = null
}
```

## Rate Limiting

The server rate-limits each token on `/openapi/v1` (`OPENAPI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_TOKEN`, default 60 requests/minute). The provider automatically backs off and retries on HTTP 429 using the response's `Retry-After` header.

## Schema

### Optional

- `host` (String) Dify base URL (e.g. `https://dify.example.com`). The provider calls `<host>/openapi/v1`. Can also be set via `DIFY_HOST` environment variable.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) Personal Access Token for authentication (`Authorization: Bearer` header). Create one in the Dify console under account settings → Personal Access Tokens; it must be scoped to the workspace. Can also be set via `DIFY_TOKEN` environment variable.
- `workspace_id` (String) Default workspace ID for resource operations. Can also be set via `DIFY_WORKSPACE_ID` environment variable. When neither is set, the provider resolves the token owner's default workspace from `GET /openapi/v1/account`.
